_note: Which chain node an Anthropic model uses when the catalog has no pin for it - a model newer than this build, or an engine running without a catalog. Data rather than code, so the Python and Rust ports derive the same node from the same file instead of each re-implementing the version arithmetic. Rules are ordered; the first match wins.
_bands: The chain is keyed on two independent questions: adaptive vs budgeted thinking (4.6 is the boundary) and whether top_k is still accepted (retired after Opus 4.6). Four combinations, four nodes.

rules.why: adaptive thinking AND still accepts top_k - the only band where both are true
legacy family-last ids (claude-3-5-sonnet) - all predate extended thinking

4.0 carrying a release DATE. Five digits or more is a date, not a minor - reading one as the other is exactly the bug fixed in 2.3.0, where claude-opus-4-20250514 parsed as minor 20250514 and cleared the 4.6 test
minor 0-5 that the top_k allow-list above did not claim

DOTTED slugs below 4.6. These get no top_k where the hyphenated form of the same model would - the retired allow-list only ever matched hyphens. Omitting top_k is a no-op and sending it to a model that retired it is a 400, so the asymmetry keeps this the safe side. Catalogued models are unaffected: they carry an explicit pin.

_default: Anything unrecognised is far likelier to be NEWER than this build than older, and the newest node is the fail-safe one: adaptive thinking, no top_k.
